Class Window

java.lang.Object
com.sbancuz.offscreen.window.Window
public final class Window extends Object
Owns one resizable SDL desktop window and its hosted Minecraft screen stack.

The native handle, shared graphics context, input queue, and GUI adapters all belong to this object. Creation and lifecycle operations run on Minecraft's main client thread. The synchronized capture/drain methods protect the event buffers; they do not make arbitrary window operations safe from other threads.

Three sizes coexist: SDL logical coordinates describe desktop input/window size; drawable pixels describe the actual framebuffer on a high-density display; GUI units describe Minecraft's scaled widgets. Keep conversions explicit when adding input or rendering features. Drawing happens in Minecraft's context, presentation in this window's context, and the outer rendering entry point restores Minecraft.

  • Constructor Details

    • Window

      public Window(String title)
      Creates and registers a native window without installing a root GUI. If SDL cannot show the window, construction continues and logs a warning. Minecraft's SDL bridge and primary GL context must already be initialized. Partial native creation is cleaned up on failure, and context-sharing setup is reset before returning to Minecraft's context.
      Parameters:
      title - non-null initial title bar text
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if SDL video, window, or shared-context creation fails

    • Window

      public Window(String title, @Nullable WindowChrome appearance)
      Creates a window with optional custom chrome and per-pixel alpha capability. Native Windows chrome remains the default when appearance is null.
      Parameters:
      title - native title
      appearance - optional custom caption, with its own opacity and controls
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if the native platform cannot create/configure the window

    • destroy

      public void destroy()
      Releases input, GUI adapters, graphics objects, native context/window, and event storage. Reentrant or repeated calls return immediately. GUI and presentation cleanup failures are logged while later cleanup stages are still attempted. Prefer the public API's close method for immediate synchronized-session release.

      Primary resources are deleted with Minecraft current. The presentation FBO is deleted with this window current, before destroying that context. Returning to Minecraft precedes deleting the secondary context so the client can continue.

    • tryRenderFrame

      public void tryRenderFrame()
      Services closure or draws one rate-limited frame, then restores Minecraft's context. Called by the driver at render-tick end. Closed windows and frames before their presentation deadline do no rendering work.

    • guiScale

      public void guiScale(int scale)
      Pins text and GUI geometry to a stable integer pixel scale across resizes. Call on the client thread. Zero restores Minecraft's automatic/configured scaling. A scale of one keeps each bitmap-font pixel one drawable pixel wide; this does not scale a captured image or change the desktop window size.
      Parameters:
      scale - zero to follow Minecraft, or a fixed scale from one through sixteen
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if outside the supported range

    • capture

      public void capture(long eventPtr)
      Copies an SDL event belonging to this window before the native callback returns. Held-state arrays update immediately; most events wait in a bounded ring for the next frame. Overflow drops the oldest ring entry. Text is decoded into owned Java storage immediately instead of retaining SDL's temporary pointer.
      Parameters:
      eventPtr - valid SDL_Event address during this call; never retained

    • setChrome

      public void setChrome(@Nullable WindowChrome appearance)
      Installs custom chrome or returns to the native title bar. Use the appearance constructor when independent caption transparency is needed: per-pixel alpha is a creation capability. Title-bar button visibility does not disable OS shortcuts or programmatic closure.

      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if closed, unsupported, or transparency was not enabled at creation

    • setIcon

      public boolean setIcon(BufferedImage image)
      Copies an image into this native window's icon. The caller retains the Java image. Alpha is preserved; SDL copies the pixels before temporary native memory is freed. Call on the client thread. No GL context or screen state changes.
      Parameters:
      image - non-null image, from 1 to 1024 pixels on each axis
      Returns:
      true if SDL accepted the icon, false for a closed window or unsupported platform
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the image dimensions exceed the icon limit

    • setFocusState

      public void setFocusState(boolean focusState)
      Focus state maintained by the input router from native focus events.

      Assigning this flag changes the recorded state used by isFocused(). It does not ask the operating system to focus or raise the desktop window.

      Parameters:
      focusState - new recorded focus state
